# FloatingTypePayoff native oracle

- Generated by `generate.py` through installed native QuantLib 1.43 SWIG.
- Both call and put invoke the actual two-input payoff overload.
- The generator also verifies the one-input `floating payoff not handled` error.
- TSV columns store IEEE-754 f64 bits as 16 hexadecimal digits, preserving signed
  zero, subnormals, infinities and NaN classifications without decimal rounding.
- Tests require exact nonzero, non-NaN output bits. NaN sign/payload is not
  contractual. The installed wheel canonicalizes zero results to positive zero;
  zero results compare numerically, with separate exact-bit tests retaining local
  source intrinsic-first `std::max` negative-zero behavior. No tolerance is used.
- 28 input pairs per option type: 56 native payoff values.
- The local reference source is independently inspected; it is not claimed to
  be the source tree used to build the installed QuantLib 1.43 binary.
